claim: An individual-participant-data meta-analysis of 46 studies (450 MRgLITT patients with drug-resistant epilepsy) found 240/415 (57.8%) non-callosotomy patients seizure free at last follow-up (median follow-up 19.0 months); CCM and MTS/atrophy predicted seizure freedom, nonlesional MRI and generalized semiology predicted earlier recurrence.

bibliographic_record.authors: Chen JS, Lamoureux AA, Shlobin NA, Elkaim LM, Wang A, et al.
bibliographic_record.title: Magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis

supporting_passage: Overall, 240 (57.8%) of 415 patients (excluding palliative corpus callosotomy) were seizure-free at last follow-up.
passage_location: Abstract (unstructured), results sentences. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 36824029; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/36824029; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: systematic review + IPD meta-analysis (mixed-effects Cox and logistic regression); databases searched 2010-01-01 to 2021-02-06
population_and_design.population: drug-resistant epilepsy, mixed ages (mean age 29.5 +/- 18.1 y) and etiologies; includes paediatric and extratemporal cases

endpoint.reported_endpoint: seizure freedom at last follow-up; time to seizure recurrence
endpoint.meets_protocol_followup_ge_12mo: partially (median meets; some individuals may fall below 12 months -- to_verify)

reported_observation: 57.8% seizure free at last follow-up; median follow-up 19 months; complications 8.5%.
author_inference: MRgLITT particularly effective for well-circumscribed lesional DRE (CCM, MTS/A), less effective in nonlesional or diffuse-network cases.
overlap_note: IPD pooled from small published series (case series typically); overlaps with patients in Kerezoudis 2020, Ekman 2024 and others in this family; do not count as independent.
